subject: Post-demo: CareAtlas eval specs, dataset format & next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: CareAtlas eval specs, dataset format & next steps

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and a concrete plan to get a Customer-Specific Eval running on Redwood: please see items below and let me know if anything should change.

1) Goal: validate model fit for clinical triage summarization use case (short clinical notes -> structured summary + triage tag). Primary success metric: human-annotated relevance/accuracy >= 85% on the test sample and no regression on hallucination-type errors vs your baseline.

2) Recommended model candidates to evaluate on Redwood (we'll run side-by-side):
   - Llama-2-13B-chat (q4f16 quantized) — strong instruction-following baseline
   - Redwell-Instruct-11B (v2) — cost efficient with tuned medical prompts
   - OpenMed-7B-instruct (fp16) — check for latency/throughput tradeoffs

3) Evaluation artifacts I'm attaching / linking:
   - careatlas-eval-template.csv (attached) — single-file CSV with columns: sample_id, prompt, context, gold_response, category, blind_label_id
   - redwood-eval-runbook.pdf (attached) — run commands, env vars, scoring pipeline examples
   - sample prompt set (link in related_links) — a curated 200-sample seed for initial pass

4) Dataset format and requirements (short checklist):
   - CSV UTF-8, header row present, no nested JSON fields in any cell
   - context column can contain up to 2048 characters; we recommend truncating at sentence boundaries
   - gold_response must be the canonical expected output (plain text), not an annotation diff
   - Include 2 columns for automated scoring: expected_label and expected_risk_tier when applicable

5) Scoring rubric (automatic + human-in-the-loop):
   - Automatic: exact-match rate for structured fields, token-level F1 for extracted entities, and an aggregated composite score
   - Human: 5-point Likert for clinical correctness, hallucination flag (Y/N), and severity if flagged
   - Regression checks: we will compare model outputs to your historical baseline set (if provided) and run hallucination-oriented tests (contradictory context, missing data prompts)

6) Size & sampling plan:
   - Start with 2k examples: 1.5k for automated scoring + 500 for human review (random stratified by category)
   - If initial variance is high, we can expand the human review pool to 1k

7) Security & data handling:
   - For PII PHI: we recommend you either pseudonymize before upload or use our Private deployment path (let us know if you prefer a VPC upload)
   - All artifacts uploaded to Redwood will be scoped to your account; retention follows the contract but can be shortened on request

8) Timeline & owners:
   - You: deliver a 2k CSV (use attached template) by Dec 7
   - Us (Jonas + Marissa): spin up the eval workflow and provide initial run results within 5 business days of receipt
   - Ben: will send a one-page pricing estimate and proposed SOW changes for dedicated evaluation capacity

9) Next steps (action items):
   - Lena: confirm dataset delivery method (S3 presigned link or secure upload) and whether you want human review in-house or via Redwood-run panel
   - Marissa: will follow up with onboarding checklist and eval job template
   - Ben: will circulate the SOW and pricing line items

Attached: careatlas-eval-template.csv, redwood-eval-runbook.pdf, SOW-draft-careatlas.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on another 30m if you want to walk through the template together.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Lena —

Answers inline and next steps.

1) Gold_response: free text is fine for the summary section. For downstream scoring we recommend adding discrete columns for the critical structured outputs (e.g., triage_code, chief_complaint_code). That lets us run exact-match and token-F1 in parallel. If you cannot produce discrete fields, we can canonicalize common patterns with a small mapping layer, but that will add ~1 business day to prep.

2) Private deployment lead time: Ben is correct — typical is 3 business days. If you share your IT contact + IP range today, we can start the VPC peering process. For the initial eval we can also accept pseudonymized S3 data to avoid the VPC step and still run everything inside your account sandbox.

Human review instructions: attached as page 6 of the runbook (redwood-eval-runbook.pdf). Summary: blinded reviewer view, Likert 1-5 for clinical correctness, binary hallucination flag, comment field for edge cases. Since you have a nurse panel we recommend Redwood do sampling + QC only; you can run the full review internally to keep control of PHI.

Next concrete items:
- Lena: S3 presigned link to dataset (or IT contact for VPC) by Dec 6
- Marissa: will share the eval job template and onboarding checklist by EOD tomorrow
- Ben: please finalize pricing in HubSpot and attach SOW

I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up for Dec 8 to review the first run.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Jonas
